significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that an internal evaluation-awareness feature causally modulates refusal and that the resulting "eval-inflation gap" varies with safety fine-tuning: a form-(iii) ordering across evaluation versus deployment framing and checkpoints, supported by a form-(ii) causal mediation claim. This would establish both a behavioral phenomenon—benchmark refusals systematically exceeding deployment-framed refusals—and a mechanism that decomposes apparent safety into evaluation-conditioned and framing-independent components, thereby constraining how refusal-direction findings such as Arditi et al. (2024) and behavioral evaluation-awareness results such as SAD (Laine et al., 2024) should be interpreted. Verified-false is also informative because it would rule out evaluation-awareness as a causal explanation for refusal inflation, rather than merely failing to locate a representation; the explicit assertions that the feature "causally raises the refusal-direction projection" and that coupling "grows with safety fine-tuning" make the branches distinguishable. After topic substitution, generic mechanistic LLM-safety importance would not retain this score: the above-median value comes specifically from linking evaluation awareness, refusal behavior, benchmark distortion, and fine-tuning in one causal decomposition.

reach.justification: The claim hands over two named handles: the measurable "eval-inflation gap" and a cheap "deployment-framing" probe or evaluation protocol for de-biasing safety benchmarks. This is primarily ex ante because auditors could apply the protocol during pre-deployment evaluation and gate or reinterpret a model before shipping, rather than only explain a harmful response afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted conclusion predicts a transferable relation—evaluation framing raises refusal, suppressing evaluation awareness raises harmful compliance, and coupling increases with safety fine-tuning—although its quantitative magnitude and applicability beyond prompt-simulated deployment would still require recalibration. The downstream users therefore include safety evaluators and deployment gatekeepers, not only mechanistic-interpretability researchers; after topic substitution, this reach remains above the median because the claim supplies a specific benchmark-correction diagnostic rather than merely restating the goal of safer LLMs.
